messages.subject: CFA and measurement invariance
parts:
Hi  all

I have constructed a 25 -items measurement scale for the assessment of risk management quality in companies over three years. The responses to items are not collected from a survey but are objectively obtained from public documents of  companies (annual reports, websites....)

I'm interested in adressing the validity of the measure in a longitudinal context. My approach is the following

1- conduct a CFA across-each time point
2- test for measurement invariance (configural, metric scalar and strict invariance)

BUT I'm wondering Is it meaningful to test for metric and scalar invariance in the case where items are objectively answered and not based on answers from survey participants.
 in fact gamma change refers to a change in how examinees understand the construct of interest and beta change refers to how they duse the response scale differently across time-points.
the answers to items are objectively answered from public sources and not from surveys. So in my case is it more plausible to test only for configural invariance??

THANK you for your precious help.

Rania

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: CFA and measurement invariance
parts:
Hi, Rania

You should test for metric ans scalar invariance (I never recommend strict). A couple of reasons I would say, first is in fact there are not invariant problems due to the source of the data them the model will just pass the tests and you will be able to do latent parameter comparisons (means, variances), is a testable hypothesis, always better to test for it instead of assuming it. Second, the description that you gave is kind of an interpretation, technically, the factor loading invariance tests the structure of the shared variance between indicators, I dont think that the items came from websites etc is related to the correlation between items. The intercept invariance looks into intercept shifts, also I dont see it related to the source of the data. 

In summary, my point of view would be that the source of the data is not necessary related to its behavior, and you can always test these hypothesis

Hope this helps

-- Mauricio
